description: Agent Consent: submit the grant’s onward rule and one planned transfer: the grant with its id, what it says about passing the data on (barred, to named recipients, with notice, with fresh consent, or allowed), the recipients it names, what it says about passing the work to a sub-agent (barred, to named ones, or allowed) and its wording, read for wording that bars onward sharing such as never shared or not sold, or opens it such as our partners; and the transfer with the recipient, its kind (a third party, a sub-agent, a processor, an affiliate or the principal), the data that would pass, whether the recipient keeps to the grant’s purpose, whether it may pass the data on again or keep it after the task, whether the principal was told or agreed, and what binds the recipient to the grant. The signed report gives the rule that applies (the sub-agent rule for a sub-agent, else the onward rule, else wording that bars sharing) with where it came from, the transfer, and each condition (onward rule, recipient named, principal told, fresh consent, same purpose, no onward passing, deleted after the task, bound in writing) as met, unmet, unstated or not_required, with counts, and names a transfer the grant bars: a barred transfer, a recipient the grant does not name where it names recipients, no fresh consent where the grant requires it and a recipient free to pass the data on where the grant does not allow it; then the principal not yet told where the grant requires it, onward sharing opened only by wording, a recipient free to use the data for another purpose or keep it, nothing in writing binding the recipient and unbounded onward passing, with the fix for each. Returning data to the principal is always within the grant. This reads one transfer under the original grant: where stored memory can cross to another agent, tool or principal is wever_memory-sharing-check, what a handoff format carries is wever_context-transfer-check, the access a receiving agent gets is wever_handoff-scope-check, authority passed down a chain of delegations is wever_delegation-chain-check and who can see an agent’s traces and logs is wever_observability-access-check. Verdict consent_transfer_barred, consent_transfer_conditional, consent_transfer_unspecified or consent_transferable. POST /api/consent-transfer-check. Reads only the recorded consent material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, sharing, configuration change or external write; no principal is contacted, no consent is requested, recorded, renewed or withdrawn and no data is used, moved or deleted. Agent Consent reads the grant the principal gave before the agent uses data or acts on it: whether the grant covers this use, whether it is still in force, whether it was withdrawn, whether the record proves it, what it was given for, whether the data may pass on and whether fresh consent is due. It is not the agent’s authority to act (wever_authority-scope-check reads an agent’s access list against the authority grant its operator gave it; a consent check reads the grant the principal gave over their own data: authority is not consent, and consent is not authority), not a mandate (the wever_mandate tools, wever_mandate-issue, wever_mandate-amend, wever_mandate-revoke and wever_mandate-draft, issue and change what an agent may trade or spend for a principal; a consent check reads what the principal agreed may be done with their data and changes nothing), not a data sample (wever_data-evidence-check reads a dataset sample’s fields and types; a consent check reads the permission behind using the data, not the data itself), not terms against a purchase (wever_terms-match-check reads purchases already made against their governing terms; a consent grant is the principal’s permission, not a seller’s terms), not a promise (the wever_commitment checks read what the agent promised; consent is what the principal granted, and an agent’s promise never stands in for it) and not an objective (the wever_goal checks read the objective the work serves; a consent check reads whether the principal’s grant allows the work at all). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-consent-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-consent/.

onward.description: What the grant says about passing the data on: barred, to named recipients, with notice, with fresh consent, or allowed.

sub_agents.description: What the grant says about passing the work to a sub-agent: barred, to named ones, or allowed.

text.description: The grant as worded, read for wording that bars onward sharing, such as never shared, or opens it, such as our partners.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

bound_by.description: What binds the recipient to the grant, such as a processing agreement or the delegation record.

fresh_consent.description: The principal agreed to this transfer.

keeps.description: The recipient may keep it after the task.

kind.description: A third party, a sub-agent, a processor, an affiliate or the principal.

notice_sent.description: The principal was told before the transfer.

passes_on.description: The recipient may pass it on again.

recipient.description: Who would receive the data or permission.

same_purpose.description: The recipient uses it only for the purpose of the grant.
